Programme Outline

Awarded and developed by: The University of Sydney, Australia

The Bachelor of Nursing (Post-Registration) programme is accredited by the Singapore Nursing Board.

The Bachelor of Nursing (Post-registration) has been developed to equip you with the knowledge, critical thinking skills and research understanding to take your career to a higher level. Eligible graduates have the opportunity to enrol in a two-year Bachelor of Nursing (Honours) programme, which prepares you for a career in research and entry into a PhD. 

The main objective of the programme is to enable you to be more confident in your role as a nurse and provide excellent nursing care.
 

Experience Australia through the Beyond Borders initiative — a unique opportunity where global learning intersects with cultural immersion in the vibrant city of Sydney.

This optional, transformative, self-funded programme invites students enrolled in the Bachelor of Nursing (Post-Registration) to collaborate with nursing and dietetic peers from around the world. Over the course of one week at Sydney Nursing School, participants will engage with insightful presentations on Australia's healthcare system, professional nursing practice, and the cultural dimensions of Australian food and society. The programme also includes guided exploration of the historic University of Sydney campus, visits to local healthcare settings, and excursions to Sydney's most iconic landmarks - including the Sydney Opera House, Harbour Bridge, and a scenic ferry ride to Manly. Through these experiences, students will gain a rich understanding of Australia's diverse cultural and multicultural landscape. Beyond Borders fosters meaningful academic exchange, professional growth, and lasting global connections.

Learning Outcomes

Upon successful completion of this programme, you will:

  1. Gain greater understanding of the role of nursing in healthcare globally. 
  2. Gain greater appreciation of the value of research to practice and an ability to translate research into practice. 
  3. Develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills in relation to nursing practice. 
  4. Develop greater leadership skill in clinical and professional nursing. 

Further Studies & Career Prospects

This programme provides students with a strong foundation in the discipline of nursing and equip them to progress to the Bachelor of Nursing (Honours), postgraduate coursework study and doctoral work.  

A Bachelor’s degree is the springboard for further study and the pursuit of a career in advanced nursing practice, research, education, or ward management.

Candidature Period:

Part-time 1-year: Students are required to complete the programme in 2 years.

Part-time 2 years: Students are required to complete the programme in 4 years.

There will not be any refund should the student fail to complete the course within the maximum allowed period.

Students who exceed their candidature period will not be allowed to remain in the programme, unless an extension to the candidature period is approved by the University.

Curriculum

Structure

  • The programme is delivered in Singapore in a block mode. Blended learning includes Face-to-face teaching for lectures and tutorials and supported by online learning. 
  • Students require access to the Internet on a regular basis for eLearning.  
  • The programme is fully taught by The University of Sydney Susan Wakil School of Nursing and Midwifery academics
    View a list of lecturers’ teaching modules (PDF 415 KB)
  • Each lecture is typically 3 hours held on weekdays late afternoon and/or evenings. Each tutorial or clinical laboratory session is typically 2 to 3 hours. 
  • Minimum class size to commence: 90 students 
    In the event that the minimum number is not met, the intake may not commence. The student shall be informed within one month before programme commencement. 
  • Average teacher-student ratio: 
    • (1-year programme) 1:41 
    • (2-year programme) 1:40 

Show more Show less

Assessment & Attendance

  • Each unit of study has a number of assessments. These include individual / group assignments, essays, presentations, case studies, formal reports, online activities / quizzes, worksheets, research activities and exams.  
  • Exams are usually held during the University’s allocated examination periods. All examinations are normally held on weekdays. 
  • Students are required to achieve an overall minimum pass of 50% for each study unit; however, the minimum pass mark may vary in some units. 
  • To achieve a minimum grade of pass, students are required to: 
    • submit all assignments and attend exams
    • meet any eLearning participation requirements where applicable
    • achieve the stated overall minimum pass mark in each unit of study
    • comply with on-campus attendance requirements
    • comply with assignment submission requirements including presentation and academic honesty 
  • Attendance requirement: 90% 

Show more Show less

Requirements to Graduate

  • Students who successfully complete all academic requirements of the programme will be awarded the Bachelor of Nursing by the University of Sydney, Australia.
  • A degree conferral ceremony will be held in Singapore.

Admission Criteria

Accepted Entry Qualifications

The following qualifications are accepted:

  • Diploma in Nursing from Nanyang Polytechnic or Ngee Ann Polytechnic, Singapore; OR
  • Diploma in Nursing from an approved institution; OR
  • Certificate in Nursing from the Singapore School of Nursing or equivalent

Applicants must also:

  • Hold a current registration with Singapore Nursing Board; AND  
  • Meet satisfaction of English language proficiency requirements as detailed in the University of Sydney's Coursework Policy

 
Applicants with international qualification are required to provide evidence of proficiency in English Language, reviewed on a case-by-case basis.

The University of Sydney undertakes selection for admission to the course. Applicants for the 1-year course are advised not to attempt to maintain full-time employment while completing the course. Sydney Nursing School considers a full-time workload will preclude students from satisfactorily meeting the academic requirements of the course. However, the level of employment a student wishes to maintain during the course is at the student’s discretion.
